findings.title: Workflow recommendation shells out to pwsh with an unvalidated repo path

evidence.source: xray file inventory plus a targeted read of capability_inventory.rs
evidence.note: Command::new("pwsh") receives options.repoPath after only an is_dir() check; the path is not canonicalized or bounded to the artifact root.

findings.problem: advisory.workflow-recommend builds a pwsh Command using the caller-supplied repoPath option after only an is_dir() check. It does not canonicalize the path or bound it to the artifact root or an allow-listed directory set before the external process starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller with request-construction access supplies a repoPath outside the intended workspace, such as a mounted directory containing unrelated material. The legacy facade script runs against that path and its stdout is trusted as a workflow proposal, so the returned proposal can carry details about a directory the caller was never meant to reach.
findings.minimal_fix: Canonicalize repoPath and reject any value that resolves outside the configured artifact root before constructing the pwsh Command.
findings.long_term_fix: Replace the PowerShell facade invocation with the in-process Rust recommendation path once it reaches parity, removing the external-process boundary entirely.
findings.regression_test: Add a capability_inventory test asserting advisory.workflow-recommend returns AdapterError::InvalidOptions when repoPath resolves outside the artifact root.
